problems.explain: Move one root across first, so that squaring leaves only one: √x = √(x + 1) + 1. Square both sides: x = x + 1 + 2√(x + 1) + 1, since (√(x + 1) + 1)² has a middle term, 2 · 1 · √(x + 1). The x's cancel: 2√(x + 1) = −2, so √(x + 1) = −1. A square root is never negative, so nothing works. (Squaring again gives x = 0, but then √x = 0 while √(x + 1) + 1 = 2: it is extraneous.) So no solution.
